prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: دورات تدريبية معتمدة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "اسم الدورة" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 250px
  col 2: header "المدة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 168px
  col 3: header "المدرب" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 105px
  col 4: header "الوصف" · longest unbreakable word 73px · one-line width 1420px
  col 5: header "الرسوم" · longest unbreakable word 43px · one-line width 70px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"good","why":"Balanced RTL layout: course titles and fees stay readable, but the description is slightly tight and the duration breaks into three short lines."},"B":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Description gets generous width, but the fee column is too narrow: currency symbols wrap onto separate lines from amounts, disrupting numeric scanning."},"C":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Best overall balance: description is wide enough for efficient reading, course titles wrap cleanly, fees stay on one line, and no column looks wasteful."},"D":{"grade":"good","why":"Clean and readable with intact fees; the trainer column is a little over-wide at the expense of the description, but rows still scan well."},"E":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Description remains usable, but the course-name column is too narrow, breaking titles into three lines and making the table unnecessarily tall."},"F":{"grade":"bad","why":"Description is squeezed into a narrow vertical strip while the trainer column is over-wide and mostly empty, producing tall rows and destroying scan rhythm."}},"best":["C"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"Exact pixel widths are estimated visually; C and D are close, and the main judgement hinges on whether the duration column’s extra line breaks matter more than description width."}
